papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Long-term lung cancer (LC) survivors remain at risk of LC events (LCEs), including late recurrence and second primary LC, beyond 5 years after diagnosis, but the role of computed tomography (CT) surveillance beyond 5 years remains uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether CT receipt beyond 5 years after LC diagnosis is associated with LCEs and survival. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This nationwide population-based cohort study used sequential target trial emulation with monthly eligibility reassessment and time-updated propensity score matching based on data from the Korean National Health Insurance Service database. Patients diagnosed with LC from 2006 to 2019 were followed up through December 31, 2024. Long-term LC survivors were eligible for trial entry 5.5 years after diagnosis if they had no administrative evidence of active or recurrent LC, a prior LCE, or another primary cancer. Data were analyzed between January 1, 2026, and February 28, 2026. EXPOSURES: CT receipt beyond 5 years after LC diagnosis, defined as chest CT during the 1-month assessment window at each monthly trial baseline, compared with no CT receipt. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was LCE occurrence, defined by new LC-specific special copayment registration after the monthly trial baseline. Secondary outcomes were all-cause mortality, surgical resection after LCE detection, and subsequent mortality. RESULTS: The cohort of 55 694 LC survivors (mean [SD] age, 63.3 [10.9] years; 58.0% male) contributed 2 629 462 eligible person-trials. Matching yielded 583 756 person-trials per group. During a median (IQR) follow-up of 2.74 (1.16-5.18) years, CT receipt was associated with a higher incidence of LCEs (2.49% vs 1.97% per year; hazard ratio [HR], 1.28 [95% CI, 1.26-1.29]) and lower all-cause mortality rate (2.62% vs 4.33% per year; HR, 0.66 [95% CI, 0.65-0.67]) compared with no CT receipt. Among patients with an LCE, CT receipt was associated with greater odds of surgical resection after LCE (odds ratio, 1.46 [95% CI, 1.41-1.52]) and a lower subsequent mortality risk (HR, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.61-0.64]). These associations were observed more frequently among females (HR, 0.47 [95% CI, 0.44-0.49]), older adults (HR, 0.57 [95% CI, 0.54-0.60]), and never smokers (HR, 0.55 [95% CI, 0.53-0.57]). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study, CT receipt beyond 5 years after LC diagnosis was associated with increased detection of LCEs, greater use of surgical resection after an LCE, and a lower all-cause mortality rate. These findings support further evaluation of risk-adapted CT surveillance beyond 5 years in selected LC survivors.

papers.abstract_en: Accurate prediction of treatment response remains challenging in cancer. To facilitate response prediction in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), we developed PRISM, an interpretable multiscale graph-learning framework for estimating treatment-specific objective response from pretreatment H&E whole-slide images. PRISM integrated multiresolution tissue representations with a cell-level tumor microenvironment (TME) hypergraph, thereby treating higher-order microenvironmental organization as a learnable component of treatment-response prediction. Samples from 7,082 patients from four Chinese centers were screened. PRISM was evaluated across treatment specific cohorts receiving targeted therapy (T), EGFR-targeted therapy (T_EGFR), immune checkpoint inhibitor-based therapy (ICI), chemoimmunotherapy (CI), and chemotherapy (C) using patient-level internal cross-validation, independent multicenter external validation, and prospective silent validation. PRISM predicted early objective responses across prespecified systemic therapies in NSCLC. In comparison to 18 established multiple-instance learning and computational pathology baseline models, PRISM remained competitive, with numerical advantages in selected tasks. Multiscale attribution and exploratory H&E-derived TME analyses provided spatial context for model predictions. Overall, PRISM offers a morphology-based framework for estimating early response to prespecified systemic therapies and warrants further prospective multicenter evaluation.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Lung cancer screening with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) has been shown to identify lung cancers at earlier stages and to significantly reduce lung cancer mortality in prior randomized clinical trials. However, the benefit of LDCT screening for small cell lung cancer (SCLC), an aggressive subtype of lung cancer, is unclear. OBJECTIVE: To investigate the characteristics and outcomes of SCLC diagnosed after a lung cancer screening examination using a large database of Medicare beneficiaries. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: In this retrospective cohort study, Medicare data linked to the Surveillance Epidemiology End Results Program's cancer registry data were analyzed. Patients in the US aged 65 to 78 years who were diagnosed with SCLC from 2015 to 2021 were identified for analysis, with follow-up data through 2022. Patients who underwent 1 or more LDCT lung cancer screening examinations during the 12 months preceding their SCLC diagnosis were included in the screened group. All other patients were included in the unscreened group. Data were analyzed from January to August 2026. EXPOSURE: One or more LDCT lung cancer screenings during the 12 months preceding SCLC diagnosis. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcomes were stage at SCLC diagnosis and overall survival after SCLC diagnosis in the screened and unscreened groups. RESULTS: A total of 17 099 patients (median [IQR] age, 72.0 [69.0-75.0] years; 8999 [52.6%] female) met study inclusion criteria, of which 949 (5.5%) were included in the screened group and 16 150 (94.5%) were included in the unscreened group. When compared with patients in the unscreened group, patients in the screened group were significantly less likely to be diagnosed with distant disease (419 of 949 [44.2%] vs 11 376 of 16 150 [70.4%]; P < .001). Patients in the screened group also had significantly better overall survival when compared with patients in the unscreened group (3-year overall survival, 28.0% [95% CI, 24.9%-31.2%] vs 10.8% [95% CI, 10.3%-11.3%]; P < .001). Both findings were consistent in propensity score-matched analysis. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results of this cohort study of Medicare beneficiaries diagnosed with SCLC suggest that receipt of lung cancer screening was associated with a shift toward earlier-stage SCLC at diagnosis and improved overall survival.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Mucus plugging causes airflow obstruction, morbidity, and mortality in chronic respiratory diseases. Charcot-Leyden crystals (CLCs), formed from eosinophil-derived Galectin-10, are frequently observed in pathologic mucus, but their role in disease is unclear. OBJECTIVES: To define the prevalence, inflammatory context, and functional role of CLCs in mucus plugs, using acute allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA) as a model of eosinophilic muco-obstructive disease. METHODS: Airway samples from 19 patients with acute ABPA and 61 disease controls were analyzed for CLCs and Galectin-10. Paired samples from plugged and unplugged bronchial mucosal biopsies defined the spatial relationship between CLCs and inflammation. A novel mouse model demonstrated the contribution of CLCs to airway obstruction and inflammation and enabled evaluation of CLC-directed imaging and therapy. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Airway CLCs were a sensitive and specific marker of acute ABPA. CLC-containing mucus plugs were surrounded by a localized type 2 inflammatory niche, alongside eosinophils, neutrophils and extracellular traps, whereas inflammation was minimal in unplugged airways from the same patients, or plugs lacking CLCs. In mice, CLC-containing plugs induced persistent airway obstruction and local inflammation, both reduced by a crystal-dissolving anti-Galectin-10 antibody. Galectin-10 concentrations provided a quantitative biomarker of acute ABPA, while a CLC-targeted positron emission tomography tracer enabled noninvasive visualization of crystal-rich plugs. CONCLUSIONS: CLC-containing mucus plugs form focal inflammatory niches in acute ABPA, and experimental CLC deposition is sufficient to promote persistent airway obstruction and inflammation. These findings identify CLCs as a biomarker, imaging target, and tractable therapeutic target in eosinophilic muco-obstructive airway disease.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP) is a potentially life-threatening adverse event caused by anti-programmed death-1 (PD-1) and programmed death ligand-1 (PD-L1) antibodies. However, paradoxical findings have been reported regarding the association between overall survival (OS) and CIP. This study aimed to prospectively evaluate the relationship between the 2-year OS and CIP in patients receiving first-line treatment, including anti-PD-1/PD-L1 antibody therapy, using 3-month and 1-year landmark analyses. METHODS: A multicenter prospective observational study was conducted between December 2021 and November 2023 to evaluate the prognostic impact of CIP, based on timing and severity, in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). RESULTS: Although no significant difference in OS was observed between patients with and without CIP developed within 2 years or 1 year, the 3-month landmark analysis showed that patients who developed CIP within 3 months had significantly shorter OS than those who did not (median OS from the 3-months landmark: 11.1 months with CIP versus not reached without CIP; log-rank p = 0.011). In multivariate Cox regression analyses, using patients without CIP as the reference group, CIP within 3 months was significantly associated with impaired overall survival (any-grade CIP: hazard ratio [HR] = 2.22, 95% confidence interval [CI]=1.21-4.09; Grade 3-5 CIP: HR=3.37, 95% CI=1.57-7.23). CONCLUSION: This was the first prospective study to demonstrate the prognostic value of CIP. CIP within 3 months after the initiation of first-line treatment, including anti-PD-1/PD-L1 antibody, especially Grade 3-5 CIP, was associated with shorter OS in patients with NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Physical activity (PA) predicts both mortality and morbidity. Pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) is known to improve exercise capacity and quality of life, but it's impact on PA remains unclear. Likewise, it is uncertain which components of PR elicit the greatest response. AIM: To use component network meta-analysis (cNMA) to investigate the relative contribution of exercise modality and intensity, nonexercise components, type of supervision and programme duration of PR on PA and sleep behaviour for people with COPD. METHODS: Medline, Embase, Cinahl and Cochrane databases were searched with no date or language restrictions. We included randomised controlled trials with an intervention involving exercise for people with COPD that measured PA or sleep behaviour as an outcome. A random-effects additive cNMA assessed the relative effectiveness of PR components on steps·day-1. Certainty of evidence was based on Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluations (GRADE). FINDINGS: 50 studies (n=4136) reported a PA outcome and four studies reported a sleep outcome (n=638). The 34 studies measuring steps·day-1 were included in a cNMA (n=3039). PA increased following lower limb aerobic exercise (695 steps·day-1, 95% credible interval (CrI) 510-898; high certainty), strength training (390 steps·day-1, 95% CrI 63-811; low certainty), PA tracking (e.g. pedometers; 938 steps·day-1, 95% CrI 688-1480; low certainty). In-person supervised (-669 steps·day-1, 95% CrI -845--452; very low certainty) and remotely supervised (-685 steps·day-1, 95% CrI -1124--174; low certainty) programmes resulted in smaller changes in step count than unsupervised programmes. A meta-analysis of sleep outcomes was not possible due to the low number of studies reporting sleep as an outcome and heterogeneity in outcome measures used.

papers.abstract_en: Oligometastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is increasingly encountered in clinical practice, owing to advances in imaging techniques and the emergence of new therapeutic options. This manuscript presents the outcomes of a meeting of experts from Hong Kong, convened to review the evidence and provide guidance on the use of local ablative therapies (LATs) for patients with oligometastatic NSCLC harboring actionable mutations. The discussion addressed key topics, including the definitions of oligometastatic and oligoprogressive disease, criteria for selecting patients for radiotherapy and other LAT modalities, optimal radiotherapy dosage, and the sequencing and timing of LATs in conjunction with targeted molecular therapies. Guidance was also developed regarding whether to pause or continue systemic treatments during LAT, and the evidence supporting emerging biomarkers in this context was reviewed. Consensus statements were formulated using a modified Delphi approach, and several case examples were presented to illustrate the application of these recommendations in clinical management. The consensus statements from this meeting could provide an important basis for tailoring treatment for patients with NSCLC who have actionable mutations, as well as pointing out key areas to explore in upcoming research.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibition is increasingly integrated with thoracic radiotherapy in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), but checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP) remains a clinically important toxicity. Whether baseline systemic inflammation modifies the association between lung radiation dose and clinically significant CIP is unclear. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 268 patients with ESCC treated with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors; 154 subsequently received thoracic radiotherapy. Baseline systemic inflammation was assessed using the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) from a complete blood count obtained within 7 days before the first immunotherapy dose. The primary endpoint was grade ≥2 CIP according to CTCAE v5.0; grade ≥1 and grade ≥3 CIP were secondary endpoints. Multivariable Cox models evaluated clinical risk factors, and SII-by-V20 interaction analyses were performed in the radiotherapy subgroup. The grade ≥2 nomogram underwent 10-fold cross-validation, 1,000-resample bootstrap validation/calibration, and decision-curve analysis. RESULTS: In the overall cohort, 77/268 (28.7%), 29/268 (10.8%), and 19/268 (7.1%) patients developed grade ≥1, grade ≥2, and grade ≥3 CIP, respectively. In the radiotherapy subgroup, the corresponding event counts were 54/154 (35.1%), 20/154 (13.0%), and 13/154 (8.4%). High SII, thoracic radiotherapy, and COPD were independently associated with CIP, while higher BMI was protective. The association of V20 with CIP was concentrated in the high-SII subgroup, with significant SII×V20 interactions across severity thresholds. The nomogram had a C-index of 0.758 (95% CI, 0.680-0.836); the mean 10-fold cross-validated C-index was 0.74 (95% CI, 0.69-0.79), and the bootstrap optimism-corrected C-index was 0.73. Calibration and decision-curve analyses supported acceptable internal performance and potential clinical utility. CONCLUSIONS: Baseline systemic inflammation was associated with heterogeneity in the relationship between lung V20 and subsequent CIP risk. These findings support a hypothesis-generating host-dosimetry framework for risk stratification but do not establish a validated V20 threshold for treatment modification. Independent external validation and mechanistic studies are required before clinical implementation.

papers.results: 共纳入6项研究、12个产品级评估、10个商业AI系统。独立AI表现不一：部分评估显示AI超过放射科医师水平，部分显示无显著差异，1项显示AI低于个体阅片者表现且假阳性率约为其2倍。在唯一一项同一数据集上多商业产品的标准化同研究比较中，7个系统中有4个显著优于放射科医师平均AUC。独立AI AUC范围0.79至0.93，放射科医师平均AUC 0.81（95%CI 0.77-0.85）。偏倚风险问题常见，尤其见于患者选择。
papers.authors_conclusion: 在现有同行评议证据中，胸片肺结节检测的独立商业AI系统表现不一。现有证据不足以支持该类产品的整体独立部署，因所有研究均为回顾性或阅片研究，报告阈值不一致，且真实世界假阳性负担仍不确定。需要具有明确报告操作阈值、标准化比较设计与完整诊断性能的真实世界前瞻性评价。
papers.ai_note: 仅6项研究且异质性大，采用叙述性合成、无合并效应量，无法给出AI相对放射科医师的总体效应；'7个系统中4个显著优于平均AUC'来自单一研究的次要/亚组层面比较，摘要未给该比较的具体AUC或P值，不宜外推为类效应。偏倚风险（患者选择）普遍，纳入研究均为回顾性或阅片研究，操作阈值报告不一致，故性能区间0.79-0.93不可直接横向比较。结论本身为阴性/审慎结论，但作者同时引用了有利数值，需注意选择性强调。

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary nodules may be missed on chest radiographs despite their clinical relevance for early lung cancer detection. Commercial artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly available for chest radiograph interpretation, but evidence for their standalone performance remains fragmented across products, datasets, operating thresholds, and comparator designs. PURPOSE: To systematically evaluate the standalone diagnostic performance of commercially available AI software for pulmonary nodule detection on chest radiographs compared with radiologists reading alone, and to identify methodological factors shaping interpretation of the evidence. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261383905). PubMed, PubMed Central, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched. Eligible studies evaluated commercially available AI systems as standalone detectors for pulmonary nodules on chest radiographs and directly compared their performance with radiologists reading alone using an accepted clinical reference standard. Risk of bias was assessed using an adapted QUADAS-2 framework. Findings were synthesized narratively because of heterogeneity in study design, populations, reference standards, operating thresholds, and outcome measures. RESULTS: Six studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising 12 product-level evaluations across 10 commercial AI systems. Standalone AI performance varied: some evaluations showed AI exceeding radiologist-level performance, others showed no significant difference, and one showed AI below individual reader performance with approximately twice the false-positive rate. In the only standardized within-study comparison of multiple commercial products on the same dataset, four of seven systems significantly exceeded mean radiologist AUC. Standalone AI AUC ranged from 0.79 to 0.93 against a mean reader AUC of 0.81 (95% CI 0.77-0.85), indicating that performance varied among cleared products even when tested under identical conditions. Interpretation was limited by differences in operating thresholds, comparator design, reference standards, study populations, and outcome reporting. Risk-of-bias concerns were common, particularly in patient selection. CONCLUSIONS: In the available peer-reviewed evidence, standalone commercial AI systems for chest radiograph pulmonary nodule detection show variable performance. Evidence remains insufficient to support class-wide standalone deployment because all studies were retrospective or reader-study based, thresholds were inconsistently reported, and real-world false-positive burden remains uncertain. Prospective real world evaluation with clearly reported operating thresholds, standardized comparator designs and complete diagnostic performance are needed.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) are opportunistic pathogens. In recent years, the incidence of NTM diseases has increased significantly worldwide. Nontuberculous mycobacterial pulmonary disease (NTM-PD) is highly similar to pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) in clinical presentation, imaging features, and sputum smear microscopy results, which can easily cause misdiagnosis. Notably, there are significant differences between the anti-infective treatment regimens for NTM-PD and PTB; however, effective differential diagnostic methods are currently lacking, seriously limiting the standardized treatment of NTM diseases. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to distinguish NTM-PD from PTB using a visual machine learning approach. METHODS: This study employed a prospective cohort design to conduct prospective national surveillance of NTM-PD in 17 hospitals participating in the China Non-Tuberculous Mycobacteria Surveillance (CNTMS). A total of 6694 patients were included in the analysis, NTM-PD was considered a positive event. Visual models based on logistic regression (LR) and a gradient boosting framework using tree-based learning algorithms (LightGBM, LGB) were developed using important predictive features such as bronchiectasis, diabetes, and geographic region. Model performance was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, and the area under the curve (AUC). Model predictions were interpreted using SHAP (a method that explains which features drive each prediction). RESULTS: Nine characteristics, including bronchodilation, diabetes, HIV, etc., were screened as key variables for distinguish NTM-PD and PTB. The AUC values of Logistic regression and LightGBM models in the training set were 0.714 (95%CI: 0.679 ~ 0.749) and 0.862 (95%CI: 0.843 ~ 0.882), respectively. In the two external test sets, the average AUC values of logistic regression model and LightGBM model were 0.789 (95%CI: 0.728-0.851) and 0.798 (95%CI: 0.743-0.851), respectively. Nomogram visualization identified bronchiectasis, HIV infection, COPD, and geographic region as the major contributors to the predictive score. SHAP visualization revealed geographic region, diabetes, and occupation as the most influential features for model prediction. CONCLUSIONS: Logistic regression and LGB models demonstrated effective accuracy and stability in external validation, and their visualization and interpretability analyses provide auxiliary evidence for the rapid clinical differentiation between NTM-PD and PTB.

papers.results: 临床相关性：M. avium 53.8%、M. intracellulare 54.7%、M. chimaera 17.8%。三种菌种均以结节支气管扩张型病变为主要影像表现。治疗成功63.0–67.5%、培养转阴70.8–71.9%、复发27.9–29.1%、死亡14.2–19.3%，M. avium与M. intracellulare之间相似。M. chimaera患者接受治疗的比例更低。摘要未报告各比例的95%CI、P值或组间检验统计量。

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) species are the leading causes of nontuberculous mycobacterial pulmonary disease worldwide. However, the clinical relevance and species-specific manifestations of MAC pulmonary disease (MAC-PD) caused by M. avium, M. intracellulare and M. chimaera remain incompletely understood. OBJECTIVE: To compare the clinical relevance, radiological manifestations and treatment outcomes associated with M. avium, M. intracellulare and M. chimaera pulmonary disease. METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies published between 2006 and 2 March 2026, identified through PubMed, Embase and Web of Science. Studies reporting adult patients with pulmonary isolates of M. avium, M. intracellulare or M. chimaera were included. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted to estimate pooled proportions for clinical relevance, radiological manifestations, treatment success, culture conversion, relapse and mortality. RESULTS: A total of 134 studies comprising 46 980 patients were included, of whom 28 858 had M. avium, 17 540 had M. intracellulare and 582 had M. chimaera. Clinical relevance was comparable for M. avium and M. intracellulare (53.8% versus 54.7%) but lower for M. chimaera (17.8%). Nodular bronchiectatic disease predominated across all species. Treatment success (63.0-67.5%), culture conversion (70.8-71.9%), relapse (27.9-29.1%) and mortality (14.2-19.3%) were similar between M. avium and M. intracellulare. However, patients with M. chimaera were less frequently treated. CONCLUSIONS: M. avium and M. intracellulare were associated with comparable clinical relevance, disease manifestations and treatment outcomes across geographic regions, whereas M. chimaera was associated with less clinically relevant disease. Improved molecular species differentiation may further clarify species-specific pathogenicity and clinical implications in MAC-PD.

papers.results: 全队列死亡率：女性10.0%（120/1,203），男性11.4%（301/2,640）。重度OSA男性vs女性HR 1.50；95%CI [1.09; 2.05]；p=0.011。轻度OSA HR 0.95；95%CI [0.61; 1.50]；p=0.850；中度OSA HR 1.09；95%CI [0.73; 1.63]；p=0.662；性别×严重程度交互p=0.110。年龄≤50岁组：男性vs女性HR 0.34；95%CI [0.14; 0.87]；p=0.024（该层各严重程度下女性死亡率均更高）。年龄>50岁组：重度OSA男性死亡风险最高，HR 1.58；95%CI [1.15; 2.18]；p=0.005。>50岁患者中治疗与死亡率降低相关：HR 0.52；95%CI [0.40; 0.67]；p<0.001。主要终点为全因死亡，按上述分层/交互分析报告；Cox模型校正年龄、肥胖、当前吸烟、糖尿病、Epworth嗜睡评分、高血压、心血管疾病、脑血管疾病。
papers.authors_conclusion: Mortality risk among patients with OSA varied according to sex, age, and OSA severity. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Sex differences in mortality among patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) remain incompletely understood. METHODS: We analyzed data from the Sleep Apnea Patients in Skaraborg (SIS) Study, including adult patients with OSA defined as an apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) ≥5 events/hour. OSA severity was classified as mild (AHI 5-14.9), moderate (AHI 15-29.9) or severe (AHI ≥30). All-cause mortality was assessed over a median follow-up of 5.9 (interquartile range 4.6-7.2) years using multivariable Cox regression adjusted for age, obesity, current smoking status, diabetes mellitus, Epworth Sleepiness Scale score, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, and cerebrovascular disease. Interaction between sex and OSA severity was tested, and analyses were stratified by age (≤50 and >50 years). RESULTS: The cohort comprised 3,843 patients with 421 deaths. Despite lower OSA severity, women had an overall mortality of 10.0% (120/1,203), compared with 11.4% (301/2,640) in men. Men had higher mortality than women in severe OSA (HR 1.50; 95% confidence interval (CI) [1.09; 2.05]; p = 0.011), whereas no sex differences were observed in mild and moderate OSA (HR 0.95; 95% CI [0.61; 1.50]; p = 0.850 and 1.09; 95%CI [0.73; 1.63]; p = 0.662; interaction p = 0.110) . In age-stratified analyses, among patients ≤50 years, women demonstrated higher mortality than men irrespective of the severity of OSA (HR for men versus women 0.34; 95%CI [0.14; 0.87]; p = 0.024), while among patients >50 years, men with severe OSA had the highest mortality risk (HR 1.58; 95%CI [1.15; 2.18]; p = 0.005). Treatment was associated with reduced mortality in patients >50 years (HR 0.52; 95%CI [0.40; 0.67]; p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Mortality risk among patients with OSA varied according to sex, age, and OSA severity. Our findings suggest potentially distinct risk patterns, with higher mortality observed among younger women and among older men with severe OSA. The findings in younger patients should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of events.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Ganfeborole and BTZ-043 are new drugs that may improve tuberculosis treatment. METHODS: In this phase 2, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned participants with rifampin-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis to receive the standard four-drug combination (isoniazid-rifampin-pyrazinamide-ethambutol; HRZE) for 24 weeks; bedaquiline-delamanid-moxifloxacin for 16 weeks; or one of 10 new four-drug combinations for 16 weeks. The new regimens contained ganfeborole, BTZ-043, or both, with combinations of bedaquiline, delamanid, moxifloxacin, pyrazinamide, pretomanid, and linezolid. The primary end point was the log10(time to positivity) slope (rate of change from baseline to week 12 in the time to Mycobacterium tuberculosis growth in a positive sputum culture). The treatment effect was assessed as the Bayesian posterior probability of superiority of each new regimen to HRZE with respect to the primary end point (results were used to select regimens for further evaluation, rather than for characterization of efficacy). RESULTS: A total of 401 participants underwent randomization; 371 were included in the modified intention-to-treat population and 400 in the safety population. We identified two promising regimens for further evaluation: ganfeborole-bedaquiline-pretomanid-moxifloxacin (BPMG) and BTZ-043-bedaquiline-delamanid-moxifloxacin (BDMT). The log10(time to positivity) slope was 0.129 log10(days) per week (95% Bayesian credible interval, 0.112 to 0.146) with BPMG and 0.142 log10(days) per week (95% Bayesian credible interval, 0.126 to 0.160) with BDMT, as compared with 0.118 log10(days) per week (95% Bayesian credible interval, 0.105 to 0.131) with HRZE, for a relative difference of 9.1% (95% Bayesian credible interval, -8.6 to 29.0) and 20.5% (95% Bayesian credible interval, 2.7 to 41.1), respectively, and a posterior probability of superiority of 0.83 and 0.99. The incidence of adverse events of grade 3 or higher was 38% in the BPMG group (none of the participants discontinued), 28% in the BDMT group (one discontinued because of a drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms), and 24% in the HRZE group (none discontinued). Bedaquiline-moxifloxacin-pyrazinamide-BTZ-043 was discontinued because of hepatotoxic effects. CONCLUSIONS: In this trial, two four-drug regimens, one with ganfeborole and one with BTZ-043, showed evidence of potential efficacy and a safety profile that did not preclude progression to further evaluation. (Funded by Innovative Medicines Initiative 2 Joint Undertaking and others; PARADIGM4TB ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06114628.).

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Severe COVID-19 is characterised by maladaptive host inflammation. In the SAVE-MORE trial (EudraCT no. 2020-005828-11; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04680949), suPAR-guided anakinra treatment reduced mortality and progression to severe respiratory failure (SRF), but the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. METHODS: We performed longitudinal proteomic profiling (Olink Inflammation panel, 67 proteins) in 587 SAVE-MORE participants (400 treated with anakinra and 187 with placebo), of whom 453 had samples at all three time points (baseline, Day 4, and Day 7). Analyses aimed to (i) identify baseline predictors of SRF, (ii) define inflammatory trajectories using mixed-effects models, and (iii) characterise proteomic changes at SRF onset. Cox models identified prognostic markers, validated in an independent anakinra-treated cohort from the SAVE trial (n = 153). FINDINGS: Multivariate Cox regression models adjusted for sex, age, BMI, and dexamethasone treatment showed that baseline IL-6 concentrations predicted SRF across both treatment arms (placebo HR = 1·99, CI: 1·31-3·02; anakinra HR = 2·12, CI: 1·56-2·87), while PD-L1 predicted SRF only in the placebo group (HR = 2·75, CI: 1·79-4·24). Anakinra allocation was associated with changes in inflammatory trajectories related to SRF progression. Patients developing SRF showed sustained activation marked by elevated concentrations of IL-6, MCP-1/3, EN-RAGE, and PD-L1, whereas SRF-free patients had higher levels of proteins linked to regulatory and adaptive immunity, including CD6, CD244, TRAIL, TNF-B, and FLT3L. Event-aligned analyses showed an acute inflammatory surge at SRF onset involving IL-6, CXCL5, OSM, and VEGFA, which was significantly attenuated by anakinra. Results were further confirmed in the SAVE cohort. INTERPRETATION: Progression to SRF was associated with an inflammatory amplification programme involving cytokine, chemokine, tissue-injury, and immune-checkpoint pathways. Anakinra allocation was associated with smaller changes in proteins associated with inflammatory amplification and acute inflammatory changes accompanying respiratory deterioration. These findings provide biological context for the clinical benefit observed in the SAVE-MORE trial. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The influence of germline genetics on the molecular transition from lung to tumor and different transcriptional patterns of tumors remains underexplored. Additionally, little is known about the genetic contributions to lung cancer relapse and mortality following surgery. METHODS: The transcriptional transition from non-affected lung tissue to tumor was investigated using an extended eQTL approach. Associations between variants and expression differences in tumors relative to matched surrounding lung tissue were examined in 515 surgical cases of lung adenocarcinoma. We also used Cox regression in a genome-wide association study to identify variants associated with survival (n = 3472) and relapse (n = 3369) in patients with NSCLC. RESULTS: The number of significant eQTL was approximately threefold lower in tumor than in lung tissue. Variants that showed differential cis-regulatory control on expression between lung and tumor tissues were more frequently located in bivalent or distal regulatory elements. Those variants altered the transcription factor binding landscape and the expression of genes that are differentially expressed in tumors. Co-expression modules derived from WGCNA identified module-QTLs and putative regulatory signaling genes (CDK15, CD79B, CCDC80, and SCARA5) involved in immunity and mesenchymal cell fate. Differential eQTLs for three genes (NRG1, SECISBP2L, and JAML) colocalized with GWAS-nominated lung cancer risk loci. Prognostic lung cancer loci identified 6p22.3-MBOAT1 and 16p13.3-RBFOX1. CONCLUSIONS: The lung-to-tumor transcriptomic transition is characterized by an attenuated contribution of germline variants. Differential eQTLs inform differences in gene expression between lung and tumor tissues, implicate putative cancer-related genes and pathways, and identify target genes underlying GWAS loci.

papers.title_zh: 托珠单抗用于风湿病相关间质性肺病急性加重（AE-RD-ILD）的单中心前后瞻观察性队列：24周研究者定义复合临床应答率80.8% vs 13.9%，但为非随机设计且人群以抗合成酶综合征为主
papers.title_en: Tocilizumab for acute exacerbation of rheumatic disease-associated interstitial lung disease: a real-world comparative cohort study.
papers.authors: Xu W, Ma Y, Zhang D, Wu W, Sun S, Guo R, Chen Z, Fu Y et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Rheumatology, Renji Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, Shanghai, China.
papers.results: 24周临床应答（CR）率：托珠单抗组80.8%（21/26）vs 对照组13.9%（5/36），p<0.001；风险比RR 5.82（95% CI 2.52-13.40）；校正后风险比HR 10.43（95% CI 3.71-29.28）；在处理竞争风险、保证时间偏倚及附加混杂因素的敏感性分析中结果一致。次要终点：累积泼尼松剂量3955 vs 5005 mg（p=0.016）；最低维持剂量10.0 vs 15.0 mg/day（p<0.001）；停氧比例76.9% vs 30.6%（p<0.001）；CT评估的ILD范围缩小20% vs 15%（p=0.045）。新发急性加重事件及死亡或肺移植数值上较少但无统计学差异。感染：至少1次感染23.1% vs 38.9%（p=0.272）。随访期内7例对照患者因反复或进展性呼吸系统疾病后续交叉改用托珠单抗。
papers.authors_conclusion: 托珠单抗与AE-RD-ILD更高的短期客观复合临床应答及改善的呼吸和糖皮质激素节约结局相关；这些发现支持在选定患者中进一步评估IL-6受体阻断，但非随机设计与研究者自定义终点需谨慎解读；因队列主要由抗合成酶谱系疾病患者构成，发现主要适用于该表型，不应不加警惕地外推至RA-ILD、SSc-ILD或其他RD-ILD亚型。
papers.ai_note: 主要终点为研究者自定义、未经验证的客观复合临床应答，且固定时点（24周）二分类终点却报告HR，指标解释存疑；非随机设计下适应证混杂未充分排除（对照组7例后续改用托珠单抗提示治疗选择与疾病严重度/难治性相关），敏感性分析虽提及但摘要未给出具体混杂变量与残余偏倚评估；样本量小（26 vs 36），死亡/移植与新发AE等硬终点未达统计学差异，长期结局证据不足；感染安全性比较把握度低（p=0.272），不能据此认为安全性等同或更优；人群以抗合成酶谱系为主，外推性受限（作者已自述）。

pico.p: 住院的AE-RD-ILD患者，托珠单抗组n=26，对照组（糖皮质激素为基础的常规免疫抑制、未用托珠单抗）n=36，共62例；研究期2023年1月—2024年12月
pico.ic: 托珠单抗（联合糖皮质激素为基础的治疗） vs 糖皮质激素为基础的常规免疫抑制、不含托珠单抗

papers.reason: 影响AE-RD-ILD急性期是否加用IL-6受体阻断及糖皮质激素减量策略的临床决策，并为后续RCT的主要终点选择与人群分层（抗合成酶谱系 vs RA/SSc-ILD）提供对照基线；同时是小样本观察性研究方法学（竞争风险、保证时间偏倚处理）的可评析案例。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Acute exacerbation of rheumatic disease-associated interstitial lung disease (AE-RD-ILD) is life-threatening and is commonly managed with high-dose corticosteroids; however, no standardised evidence-based regimen has been established, particularly regarding adjunctive immunosuppressive therapy. We evaluated the effectiveness and safety of tocilizumab, an interleukin-6 receptor inhibitor, in hospitalised patients with AE-RD-ILD. METHODS: In this single-centre ambispective observational cohort study conducted between January 2023 and December 2024, patients treated with tocilizumab (n=26) were compared with controls receiving corticosteroid-based conventional immunosuppression without tocilizumab (n=36). The primary outcome was investigator-defined objective composite clinical response (CR) at 24 weeks. Secondary outcomes included glucocorticoid exposure, oxygen discontinuation, radiological change, new acute exacerbation (AE) events, death or lung transplantation, and safety. RESULTS: The 24-week CR rate was higher with tocilizumab than in controls (80.8% [21/26] vs. 13.9% [5/36], p<0.001), with a risk ratio of 5.82 (95% CI 2.52-13.40) and an adjusted hazard ratio of 10.43 (95% CI 3.71-29.28); estimates were consistent in sensitivity analyses addressing competing risks, guarantee-time bias and additional confounders. Tocilizumab was associated with lower cumulative prednisone dose (3955 vs. 5005 mg, p=0.016), lower minimum maintenance dose (10.0 vs. 15.0 mg/day, p<0.001), more frequent oxygen discontinuation (76.9% vs. 30.6%, p<0.001), and greater CT-assessed reduction in ILD extent (20% vs. 15%, p=0.045). New AE events and death or lung transplantation were numerically less frequent but not statistically significant. At least one infection occurred in 23.1% of tocilizumab-treated patients and 38.9% of controls (p=0.272). During longer follow-up, seven controls subsequently switched to tocilizumab because of recurrent or progressive respiratory disease. CONCLUSIONS: Tocilizumab was associated with higher short-term objective composite clinical response and improved respiratory and glucocorticoid-sparing outcomes in AE-RD-ILD. These findings support further evaluation of interleukin-6 receptor blockade in selected patients, while the non-randomised design and investigator-defined endpoint require cautious interpretation. Because the cohort was predominantly composed of patients with anti-synthetase-spectrum disease, the findings primarily apply to this phenotype and should not be extrapolated to RA-ILD, SSc-ILD or other RD-ILD subtypes without caution.

papers.title_zh: 对146个SCLC患者来源异种移植模型做NMF转录组分析，划分出8个生物学亚组并可投影至小鼠模型、细胞系及IMpower133患者数据
papers.title_en: Transcriptional analyses of patient derived xenograft models reveal distinct subsets of small cell lung cancer.
papers.authors: Fatherree JP, Hippe DS, Jenkins I, Hiatt JB, Wu F, Qian W, Chen X, Simpson KL et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Human Biology Division, Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center, Seattle, WA 98109, USA.
papers.results: 对146个SCLC PDX模型的基因表达数据进行NMF分析，识别出3个ASCL1主导亚组、3个NEUROD1主导亚组、1个ASCL1/NEUROD1共激活亚组和1个REST激活的低神经内分泌亚组；这些亚组在MYC家族表达、转录因子激活、抗原提呈转录程序及代表治疗靶点的细胞表面分子表达上存在差异；使用随机森林分类器将这些聚类投影至7个遗传小鼠SCLC模型、人源细胞系及IMpower133试验患者数据。摘要未报告任何关联患者疗效的数值、置信区间或P值。
papers.ai_note: 信息不足：摘要未给出与IMpower133患者应答相关联的任何效应量、CI或P值，仅称可将PDX亚组与特定模型和患者应答相联系，无法判断关联强度与统计学意义；随机森林分类器在外部数据上的投影未描述验证集/交叉验证与分类性能指标，存在过拟合与人群限定松动风险；全部证据为临床前模型推断，未验证其对患者治疗决策的影响。

pico.p: 146个小细胞肺癌（SCLC）患者来源异种移植（PDX）模型，另含7个遗传小鼠SCLC模型、人源细胞系及IMpower133临床试验患者数据（患者例数摘要未给出）

papers.reason: 为SCLC分子分型研究提供基于大规模PDX的亚组框架与可复用的模型投影工具，供后续转化研究设计参考；但未报告临床终点数值，暂不改变临床实践判断。
papers.abstract_en: Small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a neuroendocrine carcinoma characterized by early metastasis, rapid emergence of therapy resistance, and dismal patient outcomes. SCLC subtypes have been proposed based on expression of lineage transcription factors ASCL1, NEUROD1, and POU2F3 and the level of inflammation. To further discern biologically distinct subsets, we apply non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) to gene expression data from 146 SCLC patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models. We identify three ASCL1-dominant and three NEUROD1-dominant subsets, an ASCL1/NEUROD1 co-active subset, and a REST-active low-neuroendocrine subset. These subsets differ in MYC family expression, transcription factor activation, antigen presentation transcriptional programs, and expression of cell surface molecules that represent therapeutic targets. Using a random forest classifier, we project these clusters onto 7 genetic mouse models of SCLC, human cell lines, and patient data from the IMpower133 clinical trial, allowing us to link PDX-derived subsets to specific murine and cellular models and to patient responses.

papers.title_en: Base editor tiling of the PTPN11 gene identifies resistance variants to SHP2 inhibitors.
papers.authors: Ravichandran M, Dorighi KM, Martinez OE, Sodir NM, Zhu A, Passang T, Li Z, John C et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Translational Oncology, Genentech, Inc., South San Francisco, CA 94080, USA.
papers.authors_conclusion: Our study provides a comprehensive map of SHP2 mutations that reduce inhibitor sensitivity and identifies pre-existing variants that may confer intrinsic resistance to allosteric inhibitors in patients.
papers.ai_note: 全部证据为临床前筛选与生物信息学交叉比对，无任何患者疗效或耐药发生率数据；'may confer intrinsic resistance to patients' 属外推，信息不足。筛选富集突变与肿瘤突变的重叠为观察性关联，不能证明这些变异在患者中导致耐药；部分突变对TNO155比migoprotafib耐药升高为定性描述，摘要无定量数值。

pico.p: 肺癌细胞系（具体样本量/细胞系数量摘要未报告）；另交叉比对主要为晚期、未接受SHP2抑制剂治疗肿瘤的综合基因组谱数据（样本量摘要未报告）
pico.ic: 碱基编辑饱和突变筛选下的SHP2突变体 × migoprotafib 或 TNO155 处理；对照为无抑制剂处理/野生型筛选条件（摘要未明确分组细节）

papers.reason: 为SHP2变构抑制剂在肺癌中的耐药机制提供系统性突变图谱，影响未来靶向治疗患者耐药基因检测panel设计与耐药后再治疗策略的科研假设构建；但无临床终点，不直接改变当前临床决策。
papers.abstract_en: SHP2, a tyrosine phosphatase and key modulator of oncogenic signaling pathways, has emerged as a promising cancer target, but the impact of SHP2 mutations on therapy response remains unclear. Here we perform high-throughput mutagenic base editor screens in lung cancer cells to identify SHP2 mutations conferring resistance to migoprotafib and TNO155. Our screens identify numerous gain-of-function mutations associated with Noonan syndrome and various malignancies. Most resistance mutations overlap between inhibitors, although some exhibit elevated resistance to TNO155 compared to migoprotafib. Cross-referencing comprehensive genomic profiling data from predominantly advanced, SHP2 inhibitor-naive tumors reveals significant overlap between screen-enriched and tumor-associated mutations. We validate select mutations using in vitro and in cellulo assays and perform structural analyses to gain insights into the mechanisms driving resistance. Our study provides a comprehensive map of SHP2 mutations that reduce inhibitor sensitivity and identifies pre-existing variants that may confer intrinsic resistance to allosteric inhibitors in patients.

papers.title_zh: 0.55T相位分辨功能肺MRI可量化通气与灌注缺损并区分肺病患者与对照，但缺金标准验证且重复性指标参差
papers.title_en: Phase-resolved Functional Lung MRI at 0.55 T for Evaluation of Ventilation and Perfusion in Pulmonary Disease.
papers.authors: Capaldi DPI, Baria D, Deo P, Lee YJ, Su P, Miao X, Grimm R, Voskrebenzev A et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Radiation Oncology, University of California, San Francisco, 505 Parnassus Ave, San Francisco, CA 94143.

papers.abstract_en: Purpose To evaluate ventilation and perfusion in control participants and individuals with lung disease using 0.55-T phase-resolved functional lung (PREFUL) MRI. Materials and Methods In this prospective study at a single academic institution, multisection free-breathing hydrogen 1 MRI was performed with a 0.55-T scanner with a balanced steady-state free precession sequence. PREFUL analysis was used to quantify the ventilation-defect-percentage (VDP), perfusion-defect-percentage (QDP), and ventilation-perfusion-mismatch (VQM) defects. Scan-rescan repeatability was assessed in 42 participants. Statistical analyses included nonparametric group comparisons and correlations with pulmonary function test (PFT) parameters. Results A total of 67 participants (mean age ± SD: 51 years ± 19; 32 female) were enrolled between November 2022 and March 2024, including 38 with different lung diseases, some with multiple underlying diagnoses (obstructive = 20, vascular = 9, fibrotic = 14, cancer = 34 and other = 23), and 29 control participants. Compared with control participants, individuals with lung disease had greater QDP (17% vs 11%; P = .02), VDP (30% vs 22%; P = .003), and VQM defects (7% vs 3%; P = .002). VDP and VQM defects were correlated with PFT measurements, including forced expiratory volume in 1 second (ρ = -0.59, P < .001; ρ = -0.50, P = .001), forced vital capacity (ρ = -0.53, P = .005; ρ = -0.49, P = .01), and diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide (ρ = -0.53, P = .02; ρ = -0.52, P = .02). Scan-rescan analysis revealed minimal bias (P = .06-0.3), coefficients of variation between 10.1% and 37.8%, and intraclass correlation coefficients of 0.64-0.90 for the three MRI metrics. Conclusion 0.55-T PREFUL MRI provides a reproducible, noninvasive method for quantifying ventilation and perfusion defects and effectively distinguishes individuals with lung disease from control participants. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The aim of this study is to quantitatively describe the characteristics of disease progression and its influencing factors in the placebo group of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis clinical trials, and to provide evidence for the optimal design of clinical trials. METHODS: PubMed, Embase and Cochrane Library were searched for placebo-randomized controlled trials on IPF up to November 12, 2024. We conducted a time-course modeling analysis of the placebo group based on commonly reported evaluation indicators in clinical trials. Using the established model, we simulated the distribution of the placebo effect for each index under various conditions and applied this to provide a quantitative external control. RESULTS: A total of 32 studies were included. Common evaluation measures in clinical trials include all-cause mortality, forced vital capacity (FVC), 6-minute walk distance (6MWD) and Diffusing Capacity of the Lung for Carbon Monoxide (DLCO). Based on the final model, this study simulated typical effect sizes after different times of placebo intervention. Subgroup analysis showed that background treatment and gender also showed consistent trends in the effects on the above efficacy indicators. The potential utility of this model in drug effectiveness evaluation is demonstrated through a preliminary case study. CONCLUSIONS: This study established a disease progression model for the placebo group based on common evaluation indicators in IPF clinical trials. This model helps conserve valuable clinical resources for rare diseases and promotes the development of new drugs. STUDY REGISTRATION: The study strictly followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines (Supplementary Material) and was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) (registration ID: CRD42024557923).

papers.abstract_en: The ribosome, long considered an invariant actor of gene expression, recently emerged as a contributor to translational control through chemical modifications of ribosomal RNAs (rRNAs). These modifications are guided by small nucleolar RNAs (snoRNAs), which direct modifying enzymes to specific rRNA positions. Here, we report that lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) cells that are resistant to tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) reshape both their translational program and rRNA 2'O-ribose methylation (2'Ome) profiles. EML4-ALK-positive LUAD cells that are resistant to crizotinib (ALK inhibitor) exhibit reduced global protein synthesis and a change in selective translation of mRNAs, encoding proteins previously linked to resistance. These cells show concomitant reduction in SNORD104 and 2'Ome at its associated 28S_Cm1327 position. Functional studies reveal that SNORD104 depletion abolishes 2'Ome at 28S_Cm1327 without affecting basal translation or cell viability, but enhances both under crizotinib exposure. Moreover, SNORD104 knockdown attenuates caspase activation and PARP cleavage during treatment, supporting reduced cell death. Altogether, our findings support a role for snoRNA-guided rRNA modification as a novel non-genomic mechanism in early adaptive responses to crizotinib therapy in LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Intensive smoking cessation interventions (I-SCIs) are among the most effective approaches to smoking cessation. Although socioeconomic inequalities in smoking are well-established, smoking cessation outcomes among detailed educational and employment subgroups receiving I-SCI remain poorly understood. Therefore, this study aimed to examine smoking cessation outcomes by educational attainment and employment status among participants receiving I-SCI. METHODS: This nationwide prospective cohort study was conducted in Denmark and included participants aged ≥18 years from the Danish STOPbase who received an I-SCI between January 2006 and June 2023. I-SCI comprised a structured behavioural and educational smoking cessation programme of ≥5-sessions, including pharmaceutical therapy. The primary outcome was continuous cessation from smoking at 6 months, self-reported by structured interviews. RESULTS: Among 101,549 participants, 34.1% achieved abstinence at 6-months. Cessation rates showed a clear educational gradient, ranging from 38.5% among participants with long-term education to 28.2% among those with no education or primary school education. After adjustment, participants with no education or primary school education were less likely to achieve smoking cessation (risk ratio (RR), 0.76 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.70-0.83]). Employment status was also associated with smoking cessation outcomes, although the pattern was less consistent and did not show a clear socioeconomic gradient. CONCLUSION: Higher educational attainment was consistently associated with greater continuous smoking cessation success after I-SCI, whereas associations with employment status were more heterogeneous. Educational attainment showed a clearer socioeconomic gradient in cessation outcomes than employment status, although residual confounding factors and health-selection effects may have influenced the observed associations.

papers.abstract_en: Acute lung injury (ALI) is a severe inflammatory disorder with limited effective targeted therapies. Macrophage-associated ferroptotic stress contributes significantly to uncontrolled pulmonary inflammation, making it a promising therapeutic target for ALI treatment. Here, we report biomimetic macrophage membrane-coated hesperetin (HST)-magnesium (Mg2 +) nanoparticles (MM@HST-Mg NPs) that integrate inflammation-targeted delivery with ferroptosis modulation for the treatment of lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced ALI. The macrophage membrane coating enabled MM@HST-Mg NPs preferentially accumulate in inflamed lungs and be predominantly taken up by pulmonary macrophages. Compared with free HST or HST-Mg, MM@HST-Mg NPs exhibited superior therapeutic efficacy. They alleviated macrophage-associated ferroptotic stress by scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS), reducing intracellular Fe2 + accumulation, suppressing lipid peroxidation, and activating the Nrf2/HO-1/GPX4 antioxidant pathway. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) demonstrated that Mg2 + coordination enhanced the interaction between HST and Nrf2. Furthermore, Nrf2 knockdown and pharmacological inhibition confirmed that the anti-ferroptotic and macrophage-reprogramming effects of MM@HST-Mg NPs were largely dependent on Nrf2 signaling. These coordinated effects promoted macrophage polarization toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype, attenuated pulmonary inflammation, and effectively protected mice against LPS-induced ALI following early intervention. Overall, this study establishes a biomimetic macrophage-targeted nanoplatform for ferroptosis modulation and provides a rational strategy for developing immunoregulatory nanomedicines for acute inflammatory lung injury.

papers.abstract_en: COPD is characterised by pronounced regional heterogeneity in structural damage and functional impairment, leading to substantial variability in symptoms and treatment response among patients with similar spirometric severity. Conventional pulmonary function tests rely on patient cooperation and provide global measures of airflow limitation, which incompletely capture regional abnormalities and may be difficult to perform or interpret in patients with advanced disease or limited ability to cooperate. Imaging-based assessment provides objective, effort-independent, spatially resolved evaluation that complements global pulmonary function tests. Quantitative imaging allows characterisation of emphysema distribution, small-airway dysfunction, air trapping, collateral ventilation, and regional perfusion, enabling identification of physiologically inefficient and potentially dispensable lung regions. In this review, we propose that the key clinical question is not how much lung is diseased, but which regions meaningfully contribute to overall function and which may be safely excluded. These regional insights are particularly relevant to lung volume reduction, where treatment effect depends on selecting targets with high mechanical burden and low gas exchange contribution. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is an aggressive malignancy with dismal prognosis, primarily attributed to substantial tumor heterogeneity. Although the cytoskeleton is critically implicated in cancer progression, a comprehensive characterization of cytoskeleton-related prognostic genes in ESCC is still absent. METHODS: Bulk transcriptome data from public repositories were integrated with a single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) dataset for comprehensive analysis. Cytoskeleton-related candidate genes were screened by intersecting differentially expressed genes with a curated cytoskeleton-related gene (CRG) list, and expression findings were experimentally corroborated in clinical specimens via real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). Independent prognostic genes were subsequently determined through univariate and multivariate Cox regression analyses and incorporated into a risk model, which was subsequently evaluated in two external cohorts. Additional analyses covered functional enrichment, immune infiltration profiling, drug sensitivity estimation, mutational landscape characterization, and single-cell-level investigations of inferred metabolic pathway activity, intercellular communication, and differentiation trajectories. RESULTS: A total of 222 cytoskeleton-related candidate genes were identified. Among these, three genes -GABARAPL2, PDLIM2, and PPP2R2A - were established as independent prognostic factors and incorporated into a robust risk-scoring model. This model reliably partitioned patients into high- and low-risk groups with markedly divergent survival outcomes, and a similar association between the risk score and survival was observed in two external cohorts. The high-risk group exhibited distinct estimated immune infiltration, immune checkpoint expression, somatic mutation, and predicted drug sensitivity profiles. scRNA-seq analysis characterized the distribution of the prognostic genes across cell types and supported the selection of T cells for further exploratory analyses of metabolism, intercellular communication, and differentiation trajectories. CONCLUSION: This multi-omics integrative study identified and validated a CRG signature with potential prognostic value in ESCC and revealed its associations with immune microenvironment features and computationally predicted drug response patterns. These findings support the potential utility of the signature for risk stratification and provide testable hypotheses for further investigation of ESCC biology.

papers.abstract_en: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) demonstrates significant intra-tumor heterogeneity (ITH), which plays a critical role in disease progression and complicates therapeutic interventions. In the present study, we employed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to analyze cellular populations derived from stage I and stage III LUAD tumors, alongside matched adjacent normal tissues, with the objective of delineating malignant cell states and identifying tumor-propagating subpopulations. Unsupervised clustering analysis identified eight principal cell lineages, with epithelial cells predominating within tumor samples. Notably, advanced-stage tumors demonstrated a shift toward an immunosuppressive microenvironment, characterized by elevated T cell exhaustion and an increased presence of pro-angiogenic macrophages. Further stratification of malignant cells revealed eleven distinct subclusters, with stage III tumors enriched for invasive and immunosuppressive phenotypes. Pseudotime trajectory analysis identified evolutionary transitions from alveolar-like states toward squamous and stress-responsive lineages. Employing CytoTRACE to evaluate stemness independently of predefined markers, we identified subpopulations of cancer stem cells (sub-CSCs) predominantly in stage III tumors. These sub-CSCs exhibited heightened transcriptional heterogeneity and a core gene signature associated with cytoskeletal motility, immune regulation, metabolic reprogramming, and protein homeostasis. A four-gene panel derived from this signature demonstrated robust prognostic significance in independent LUAD cohorts. Collectively, these findings enhance the current understanding of stemness-driven tumor progression in LUAD and suggest potential therapeutic targets to address tumor heterogeneity.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors have become an important treatment for advanced lung cancer, but patient responses exhibit substantial interindividual variability. The tumor-associated microbiome is closely related to immunotherapy efficacy. METHODS: Tumor tissue samples from lung cancer patients receiving immunotherapy were analyzed using 16 S-5R rRNA sequencing (Cohort 1). Two core models were constructed: a deep learning-based bacterial diagnostic model (BDM) incorporating hidden layers and a Squeeze-and-Excitation block to predict immunotherapy response status, and a Cox proportional hazards (CoxPH) prognostic model to predict progression-free survival (PFS). Furthermore, four core bacterial species were selected using SHAP values, and a probe-based multiplex qPCR detection system (BDM-mqPCR) was developed (Cohort 2). RESULTS: The BDM achieved a sensitivity of 96.55% and 87.50%, specificity of 96.15% and 100.00%, and AUC of 0.989 and 1.000 in the training and validation set. The CoxPH model showed high concordance between predicted PFS curves and actual outcomes in both the training and validation sets, effectively distinguishing high-risk from low-risk patients, further providing the probability distribution of their PFS to help physicians decide whether to prepare subsequent treatment in advance or intensify monitoring. BDM-mqPCR constructed using the four SHAP-selected species achieved AUCs of 0.828 (training) and 0.869 (validation), which were lower than those of the BDM but significantly superior to Biomarker model, offering the advantages of rapidity, cost-effectiveness, and target specificity. CONCLUSION: BDM model and the CoxPH model achieved a complete assessment from whether a response occurs to how long the response lasts, providing a microbiome-driven precision tool for individualized decision-making in lung cancer immunotherapy.

papers.abstract_en: Thoracic transplantation has become increasingly complex, with new donor technologies, higher-acuity candidates and recipients resulting in expanding clinical demands and placing significant pressure on transplant coordinators (TCs) and Advanced Practice Registered Nurses (APRNs), including Advanced Nurse Practitioners (ANPs) in some international centers. The International Society for Heart and Lung Transplantation (ISHLT) convened its second Transplant Nursing Consensus Conference on April 26, 2025, in Boston, to address these pressures and develop actionable recommendations. A multi-method approach integrated 3 sources: a pre-conference international survey of transplant nursing professionals, 2 virtual international roundtables with nurses from 8 countries, and 4 facilitated in-person breakout sessions. Findings converged across sources, identifying incremental accumulation of duties without resource relief, administrative and after-hours burden, role ambiguity between TCs and APRNs, and absent career structures as dominant threats to workforce sustainability. International input revealed wide variation in roles, prescribing rights, and care models, while affirming shared priorities around retention, role clarity, work-life balance, and recognition. Seven overarching themes guided recommendations: staffing models and workload; work environment and retention; workforce roles and qualifications; professional development and impact measurement; clinical processes and protocols; technology and innovation; and patient education access. The panel endorsed acuity-driven staffing ratios, hybrid call structures with protected recovery, offloading non-clinical tasks to dedicated personnel, competency-based career ladders linked to certification and compensation, standardized nurse-led protocols with clear escalation, digital tools that reduce documentation duplication, and a universal modular patient education curriculum. These consensus statements provide an internationally informed blueprint for sustaining the thoracic transplant nursing workforce.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) circulates as two antigenically distinct subgroups, RSV-A and RSV-B, frequently alternating in seasonal predominance. Whether RSV subgroup predominance affects neutralizing immunity and how population immunity shapes subsequent subgroup dynamics, remains unclear. We analyzed multi-season RSV surveillance data and subgroup neutralizing antibody responses to characterize RSV-A/B neutralizing immunity across age groups and successive seasons. METHODS: We analyzed 41,899 respiratory samples collected through sentinel surveillance to characterize RSV-A and RSV-B circulation across five seasons (2021-2026). Subgroup neutralization was measured by live-virus neutralization assays in post-season serum samples from infants, children and adults. RESULTS: RSV-A and RSV-B alternated in seasonal predominance, with RSV-A predominating in 2021/22 and 2023/24, RSV-B in 2022/23 and 2025/26, with no clear predominance in 2024/25. In infants, the relative neutralizing activity against RSV-A and RSV-B differed across seasons, whereas adults maintained a balanced neutralizing activity against both subgroups. During the first three years of life, repeated exposure broadened antibody responses toward balanced subgroup neutralization. In the 2021/22, 2022/23, and 2024/25 seasons, lower neutralizing activity in infants was observed against the subgroup that predominated in the subsequent RSV epidemic. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate that neutralizing immunity develops from initially subgroup-biased responses after primary RSV infection toward balanced RSV-A/B neutralization with repeated exposure. Subgroup neutralizing activity in infants varied in the context of alternating RSV-A and RSV-B predominance across successive epidemic seasons. These findings provide new insights into age-dependent and seasonally varying patterns of RSV-A/B neutralizing immunity and subgroup circulation.

papers.title_zh: 利福平暴露量升高与结核预防治疗的不良事件、停药及耐受性差相关，但无肝毒性关联且缺乏疗效终点
papers.title_en: Pharmacokinetic/Pharmacodynamic Analysis of Standard- and High-Dose Rifampicin to Predict Safety, Completion, and Tolerability of Tuberculosis Preventive Therapy in the 2R2 Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.authors: Gafar F, Svensson EM, Yunivita V, Fregonese F, Fisher D, Fox GJ, Nguyen TA, Nguyen BH et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Respiratory Epidemiology and Clinical Research Unit, Centre for Outcomes Research and Evaluation, Research Institute of …
papers.results: AUC0-24 每增加 2 倍：方案定义的需永久停药不良事件 aOR 1.88（95% CI 1.25-2.81）；与 AE 无关的停药 aOR 1.42（95% CI 1.15-1.75）；可能与 AE 相关但未停药的耐受性症状 aOR 1.48（95% CI 1.18-1.86）；Cmax 呈相似模式。更高的 AUC0-24 与 Cmax 还与 1-2 级及 3-4 级 AE、皮疹/过敏/超敏反应、胃肠道不耐受及早期停药相关；与肝毒性无显著关联。基于暴露的模型在预测安全性方面较基于剂量的模型判别性能略优。缺失暴露指标用 1,000 个模拟数据集插补。
papers.authors_conclusion: 较高的利福平暴露与结核预防治疗中更差的安全性、完成率和耐受性相关。需要更大的疗效试验来确定实现足够暴露的 optimal 剂量，同时应研究治疗药物监测以避免过度暴露。
papers.ai_note: 该分析仅有安全性/完成度终点，无结核预防疗效终点，因此无法回答高剂量是否净获益，暴露-反应的临床意义需与疗效权衡后判断，作者也承认需更大疗效试验。暴露量由模型预测并经 1,000 次模拟插补而非全部实测，存在模型依赖性与测量误差风险。结论强调安全性恶化，但摘要同时报告肝毒性无显著关联，安全性结局内部不一致。剂量组间比较与连续暴露-反应混杂，个体药动学差异（如吸收、合并用药）可能同时影响暴露与不良事件，观察性暴露-反应关联不能直接推断降剂量或TDM的因果获益。

pico.p: 1,368 名成人与青少年，来自 2R2 试验；群体药动学模型基于其中 440 名参与者建立
pico.ic: 利福平 20 或 30 mg/kg/日疗程 2 个月 vs 10 mg/kg/日疗程 4 个月；按 AUC0-24 与 Cmax 暴露水平分层的暴露-反应分析

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Rifampicin-based tuberculosis preventive therapy (TPT) may shorten treatment duration, but substantial interindividual pharmacokinetic variability may lead to different safety and tolerability profiles at the same dose. We performed pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic analyses of standard- and high-dose rifampicin to predict safety, completion, and tolerability. METHODS: We analyzed data from 1,368 adults and adolescents enrolled in the 2R2 trial comparing two months of rifampicin at 20 or 30 mg/kg/day with four months at 10 mg/kg/day. A population pharmacokinetic model developed from 440 participants was used to predict rifampicin exposure for all participants. Missing exposure metrics were imputed using 1,000 simulated datasets. Exposure-response relationships were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression models fitted within imputed datasets, with coefficients and standard errors pooled across imputations. RESULTS: A two-fold increase in total rifampicin exposure (AUC0-24) was associated with higher odds of protocol-defined adverse events (AEs) requiring permanent discontinuation (aOR 1.88, 95% CI 1.25-2.81), discontinuation unrelated to AEs (aOR 1.42, 95% CI 1.15-1.75), and tolerability symptoms potentially related to AEs without discontinuation (aOR 1.48, 95% CI 1.18-1.86); similar patterns were observed for peak concentration (Cmax). Higher AUC0-24 and Cmax were also associated with grade 1-2 and grade 3-4 AEs, rash/allergy/hypersensitivity, gastrointestinal intolerance, and early discontinuation, with no significant association for hepatotoxicity. Exposure-based models showed slightly better discriminatory performance than dose-based models in predicting safety. CONCLUSION: Higher rifampicin exposure was associated with worse safety, completion, and tolerability in TPT. Larger efficacy trials are needed to determine the optimal dose to achieve sufficient exposure, alongside investigation of therapeutic drug monitoring to avoid excessive exposure.

papers.authors: Liu B, Feng J, Ren H, Wen T, Zhang G, Xu F
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Surgery, The First Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University, Xi'an, P.
papers.authors_conclusion: We outline a translational roadmap for standardized mechanical biomarkers, interpretable AI and clinician-supervised digital-twin models.

papers.abstract_en: Long-term outcomes after lung transplantation remain limited by primary graft dysfunction and chronic lung allograft dysfunction, despite improvements in surgery, immunosuppression and infection control. Mechanical injury is a complementary contributor that remains insufficiently integrated into transplant care. The lung allograft must accommodate cyclic ventilation, reperfusion shear, thoracic constraints and matrix remodeling. These forces can disrupt the alveolar-capillary barrier, amplify inflammation and activate fibrotic programmes. Here we synthesize lung transplantation through a mechanomedicine framework that links organ-scale loading, cellular mechanotransduction and clinical decision-making. We discuss how computational models and artificial intelligence (AI) can integrate ex vivo lung perfusion waveforms, imaging-derived ventilation or strain patterns, and molecular injury markers to support graft-risk assessment. We then organize mechanotherapeutic strategies by clinical readiness, from protective ventilation, size matching and extracorporeal graft support to emerging interventions targeting mechanotransduction according to cell type and loading conditions. Finally, we outline a translational roadmap for standardized mechanical biomarkers, interpretable AI and clinician-supervised digital-twin models.

papers.results: A549细胞增殖被抑制，IC50 = 3.79 µM；诱导细胞凋亡与G0/G1期阻滞；异种移植模型中显著抑制肿瘤生长，所试剂量下未观察到毒性（未报告具体数值、统计学与CI）；药代研究显示acteoside迅速转化为咖啡酸，咖啡酸全身暴露量更高（未报告具体数值）；Transwell实验证实其抑制细胞迁移（未报告数值）

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, hindered by drug resistance and metastasis. Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) drives NSCLC progression and therapy resistance, but few effective EMT-targeting strategies exist. Acteoside, a phenylethanoid glycoside has shown promising antitumor activity, but its specific mechanisms in NSCLC remain unclear. METHODS: This study aimed to define the anti-NSCLC potency of acteoside, uncover its mechanism, and appraise its translational value. In vitro proliferation assays and distinct xenografts (monotherapy and Baihe Gujin Decoction) quantified efficacy. Integrative transcriptomics, proteomics, western blot, molecular dynamics, surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assay and knockdown experiment mapped the mode of action, while in vivo HPLC-MS/MS-based pharmacokinetic (PK) profiling gauged bioavailability. Functional validation supported that acteoside inhibited NSCLC cell migration in Transwell assays. RESULTS: Acteoside, identified as the key bioactive compound in Baihe Gujin Decoction, demonstrated potent anti-NSCLC efficacy both in vitro and in vivo. It inhibited A549 cell proliferation (IC50 = 3.79 µM), induced apoptosis and G0/G1 arrest, and significantly suppressed tumor growth in xenograft models without toxicity. Pharmacokinetic studies revealed acteoside acts as a prodrug, rapidly converting to caffeic acid. Multi-omics, IL-17 pathway perturbation assay and molecular analyses supported that acteoside upregulates E-cadherin (CDH1) via IL-17 pathway inhibition, with stable binding to the E-cadherin dimer interface validated by molecular dynamics, SPR, knockdown experiment and Western blot. Transwell assays functionally validated EMT modulation and migration inhibition. These findings provide evidence for acteoside as a novel small-molecule CDH1 modulator for NSCLC treatment. CONCLUSION: Acteoside is an antitumor agent that suppresses cancer cell proliferation and induces tumor regression in preclinical models, with no overt toxicity observed at the tested doses. Mechanistically, acteoside upregulates E-cadherin (CDH1) expression and directly binds to the CDH1 protein with measurable affinity, while also modulating the IL-17 signaling pathway. Pharmacokinetic studies indicate that acteoside undergoes extensive metabolism after oral administration, with its metabolite caffeic acid reaching higher systemic exposure, suggesting a potential prodrug characteristic. These findings position acteoside as a promising candidate for CDH1-targeted therapeutic strategies in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), warranting further investigation.

papers.title_en: Self-reported decreased libido in patients evaluated for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA): Association with depressive symptoms rather than OSA severity.
papers.authors: Dramé M, Coffi M, Zabulon A, Awanou B, Andreu M, Inamo J, Duféal M, Parsemain A et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Clinical Research and Innovation, Centre Hospitalier Universitaire de Martinique, Fort-de-France, France.
papers.results: 188例纳入患者中44.7%自我报告性欲下降；平均年龄55.3 ± 15.9岁，女性占64.4%。基于DAG选择混杂因素的多变量分析中，年龄增大与性欲下降独立相关，中重度OSA仅呈临界（borderline）相关。纳入日间症状与抑郁症状的扩展模型中，较高抑郁症状评分仍与性欲下降独立相关，而OSA严重程度指标、日间嗜睡与疲劳不相关。性别分层分析中，女性中抑郁症状与婚姻/伴侣状态相关，男性中年龄为主要决定因素。性别与抑郁症状交互作用的正式检验无统计学显著性。
papers.authors_conclusion: 自我报告性欲下降在因疑似OSA就诊的患者中很常见。性欲下降似乎与抑郁症状及社会心理因素的关联较与客观呼吸疾病严重程度的关联更一致。这些发现凸显了在OSA评估患者的常规呼吸科诊疗路径中整合心理与生活质量评估的重要性。
papers.ai_note: 摘要未给出任何效应量（OR/RR）、95%CI或P值，仅用'borderline'描述中重度OSA的关联，无法判断关联强度与统计精度，信息不足。横断面设计不能推断因果，作者'appears to be more consistently associated'的表述隐含比较性推断，但两组关联均无量化指标支撑。主要结局为二分法自报性欲下降，测量粗糙且未报告信效度。样本量188例却构建了含多协变量的扩展模型、性别分层及交互检验，效能可能不足；交互检验不显著，却仍按分层结果给出男女不同主导因素的结论。单中心、64.4%为女性，代表性有限。

pico.p: 因疑似或确诊阻塞性睡眠呼吸暂停（OSA）转诊评估的患者，共188例（平均年龄55.3 ± 15.9岁，女性64.4%）
pico.ic: 采用DAG选择混杂因素的多变量logistic回归、纳入日间症状与抑郁症状的扩展模型、性别分层分析及性别×抑郁症状交互检验（均以自我报告性欲下降为因变量，无干预对照）

papers.reason: 为OSA评估人群的性功能主诉提供患病率基线，并提示性欲下降这类症状不能由呼吸疾病严重程度解释，影响呼吸科门诊对OSA患者症状归因与心理评估流程的设定；同时作为'症状与OSA严重程度不匹配'主题的阴性关联证据，可用于评估随访与生活质量干预的侧重方向。
papers.abstract_en: BackgroundSexual health complaints are frequently reported by patients evaluated for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) but remain under-recognized in respiratory care settings. The relative contributions of respiratory disease severity, daytime symptoms, and psychological factors to decreased libido in this population remain poorly understood.ObjectivesThe aim of the study was to determine the prevalence of self-reported decreased libido in patients evaluated for suspected or confirmed OSA and to identify factors independently associated with this complaint.DesignMonocentric cross-sectional observational study performed in patients referred for suspected or confirmed obstructive sleep apnea from 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025.MethodsSelf-reported decreased libido was assessed using a dichotomous patient-reported measure. Demographic characteristics, body mass index, comorbidities, OSA severity indices, daytime sleepiness, fatigue, and depressive symptoms were collected using standardized clinical assessments and questionnaires. Multivariable logistic regression models were performed to identify factors independently associated with decreased libido, including models based on directed acyclic graph (DAG) confounder selection, extended models including symptoms, sex-stratified analyses, and formal testing of sex-by-depression interaction.ResultsAmong 188 included patients (mean age 55.3 ± 15.9 years; 64.4% women), self-reported decreased libido was reported by 44.7%. In multivariable analyses based on DAG-selected confounders, increasing age was independently associated with decreased libido, while moderate-to-severe OSA showed only a borderline association. In the extended model including daytime symptoms and depressive symptoms, higher depressive symptom scores remained independently associated with decreased libido, whereas indices of OSA severity, daytime sleepiness, and fatigue were not associated. Sex-stratified analyses showed that depressive symptoms and relationship status were associated with decreased libido among women, whereas age was the main determinant among men. Formal testing of the interaction between sex and depressive symptoms was not statistically significant.ConclusionsSelf-reported decreased libido is common among patients evaluated for suspected OSA. Decreased libido appears to be more consistently associated with depressive symptoms and psychosocial factors than with objective respiratory disease severity. These findings highlight the importance of integrating psychological and quality-of-life assessment into routine respiratory care pathways for patients evaluated for OSA.

Tumor-expressed CD155 down-regulates NK-cell CD226; however, whether reduced NK-cell CD226 reciprocally modulates tumor-cell CD155 and the underlying regulatory mechanism remain unclear. METHODS: Public transcriptome datasets GSE32863 and TCGA-LUAD were analyzed. CD226-overexpressing NK92 cells and primary NK cells from CD226-knockout mice were applied in co‑culture systems with NSCLC/LLC tumor cells. Gain-and loss-of-function assays using recombinant IL-22, IL-22 neutralizing antibody and STAT3 siRNA were performed, combined with flow cytometry, RT-qPCR, western blot, ELISA and functional cytotoxicity, proliferation and invasion assays. CD226 overexpression restrained NK-cell-derived IL-22 transcription and secretion. NK-cell-produced IL-22 triggered tumor-cell CD155 upregulation via IL-22RA1-pSTAT3 signaling. CD226-high NK cells displayed stronger anti‑tumor cytotoxicity, while exogenous IL-22 impaired NK-mediated tumor killing. Murine CD226-deficient primary NK cells reproduced this regulatory circuit. CONCLUSION: CD226 overexpression restrains NK-cell-derived IL-22 and interrupts an IL-22RA1-pSTAT3-CD155 immune-evasive circuit in NSCLC. This work supports combinatorial NK-cell engineering and IL-22-targeted immunotherapeutic strategies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Research on the association between sodium‑glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT-2i) and chronic lower respiratory diseases (CLRDs) in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2DM) remains limited. This study aimed to investigate this association and examine the potential modifying effects such as age, sex, and diabetes severity. METHODS: Using the Shenzhen Public Health Data Platform, we conducted two independent target trial emulations with a new‑user active comparator design, comparing SGLT‑2i with glucagon‑like peptide‑1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) and dipeptidyl peptidase‑4 inhibitors (DPP‑4i), respectively. The primary outcome was incident CLRD; secondary outcomes included five subtypes-bronchitis, bronchiectasis, asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and emphysema. Overlap-weighted Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 1.76 years, 349 (7.95%) and 397 (9.04%) new CLRD cases occurred in SGLT-2i and GLP-1RA users, respectively. Compared with GLP-1RA, SGLT-2i use was associated with a lower CLRD incidence (HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.79-0.96), primarily driven by reduced risk of bronchitis (HR: 0.89; 95% CI: 0.79-1.00) and asthma (HR: 0.77; 95% CI: 0.58-1.01); no significant associations were found for other subtypes. Compared with DPP-4i, SGLT-2i use showed a trend toward lower CLRD risk (HR: 0.95; 95% CI: 0.91-0.99), with significant reductions for bronchitis (HR: 0.95; 95% CI: 0.91-1.00), bronchiectasis (HR: 0.86; 95% CI: 0.75-1.00), and asthma (HR: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.77-0.98). Subgroup analyses indicated significant interactions for bronchiectasis by sex (P interaction = 0.001). CONCLUSION: Compared with GLP-1 RA, SGLT-2i were associated with a significantly lower risk of CLRDs, driven predominantly by bronchitis; versus DPP-4i, the risk reduction was primarily observed for bronchitis, bronchiectasis, and asthma. The protective association between SGLT-2i use and bronchiectasis was more pronounced in females than in males relative to DPP-4i.
