papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung cancer remains a major global public health burden, characterized by high morbidity and mortality. The tumor immune microenvironment of lung cancer displays complex and dynamically changing immune landscapes, where diverse cell types collectively construct an immunosuppressive tumor ecosystem. Accordingly, boosting host immune function represents a promising therapeutic strategy to improve clinical outcomes and alleviate treatment-related adverse reactions in patients with lung cancer. OBJECTIVE: To systematically analyze the effects, efficacy, and safety of Compound Kushen Injection (CKI) combined with conventional treatment on improving immune function in lung cancer patients, providing evidence-based medical evidence for clinical practice. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in major Chinese and English databases from their inception to 25 March 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating the impact of CKI on immune function in lung cancer patients were included. Quality assessment and data extraction were performed, and statistical analyses were conducted using Review Manager 5.4 and Stata 18.0 software. RESULTS: A total of 3846 patients from 39 RCTs were included (1971 in the experimental group and 1875 in the control group). Compared with conventional treatment alone, CKI combined with conventional treatment significantly enhanced immune function, as evidenced by increased levels of CD3+, CD4+, CD4+/CD8+ ratio, and natural killer (NK) cells, and decreased levels of CD8+ cells. Additionally, this combination improved the objective response rate (ORR) and disease control rate (DCR), reduced carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) levels, improved Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) scores, prolonged 1-year overall survival, and effectively reduced treatment-related adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal reactions, myelosuppression, hepatorenal toxicity, and fatigue. CONCLUSION: Current evidence indicates that CKI combined with conventional treatment provides multiple clinical benefits for lung cancer patients. However, the limited available evidence may compromise the reliability of our conclusions. Rigorously designed multicenter double-blind randomized controlled trials with staged analyses and long-term follow-up are needed to validate these findings. All findings should be interpreted as exploratory. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261384207, identifier CRD420261384207.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The success of mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (LNP) platforms has prompted significant interest in their application against bacterial pathogens. However, adapting these platforms requires optimising host-expressed antigen structure to ensure robust immunogenicity. While membrane anchoring enhances the efficacy of viral mRNA vaccines, its application in bacterial mRNA platforms remains largely unexplored. Plague, caused by the Gram-negative bacterium Yersinia pestis, has been one of the most devastating diseases throughout human history. Despite extensive studies, there are no licenced vaccines available. METHODS: We developed a bivalent mRNA-LNP vaccine against Y. pestis, utilising the major antigens F1 and LcrV (5 μg of each mRNA). We evaluated glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI)-anchored and transmembrane (TM) variants alongside secreted native and hFc-conjugated formats to assess immunological profiles and determine protective efficacy in a murine model of pneumonic plague. FINDINGS: Membrane-tethering of F1 and LcrV antigens improved overall immunogenicity. Whereas secreted native and hFc-conjugated variants elicited predominantly cell-mediated and serological immune responses, respectively, the membrane-anchored bivalent mRNA vaccine generated a robust, protective immune response. This dual humoural and cellular immunity facilitated robust (87.5%, 7/8 mice) protection following a single-dose vaccination. INTERPRETATION: By progressing towards the single-dose biodefense benchmark prioritised by the World Health Organisation Target Product Profile, this membrane-anchored construct emerges as a promising translational candidate for a rapid-response plague vaccine. Ultimately, this study demonstrates that extending established antigen-tethering strategies to bacterial targets may be a highly effective approach for generating the potent immunity required to overcome complex bacterial infections. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is a highly transmissible respiratory infection that has caused a global pandemic. Evidence for the effect of short-term PM2.5 exposure on COVID-19 incidence varied across regions, and few studies have used advanced spatial analysis methods to examine spatial autocorrelation or clustering in these associations to improve estimation accuracy and identify highly susceptible geographic regions. METHODS: In this study, we used a novel three-stage strategy, including generalized additive model (GAM) and the newly developed estimation-error-based scan statistic (EESS) and multivariate conditional meta-autoregression (MCMAR), to fill the gap across the contiguous United States. RESULTS: We found there was significant spatial heterogeneity ( I 2 = 67.416 % , P < 0.001 ), autocorrelation ( ρ = 0.972 , P < 0.001 ), and clustering (four clusters were discovered, P ≤ 0.011 ) in the associations between short-term exposure to PM2.5 and daily reported confirmed COVID-19 cases. Considering the spatial autocorrelation and the spatial clustering effectively improved the fitting results of meta-regression. The pooled relative risk (RR) and 95% confidence intervals (95% CI) for per 10 μg/m3 increase in PM2.5 were 1.0341 and (1.0308, 1.0375). The RRs (95% CIs) for per 10 μg/m3 increase in PM2.5 were 1.0107 (1.0074, 1.0140), 1.1770 (1.1551, 1.1992), 1.0005 (0.9984, 1.0026), 1.0719 (1.0566, 1.0875), and 1.1032 (1.0798, 1.1270) in baseline and clusters 1-4, respectively. By 30 June 2022, a total of 1,761,726 (95% CI: 1,583,970-1,916,779; accounting for 2.06%, 95% CI: 1.85-2.24%) COVID-19 cases were found to be related to elevated PM2.5 exposure relative to the WHO annual mean PM2.5 guideline threshold of 5 μg/m3 across the contiguous United States. The eastern region and central region exhibited greater RR, greater attributable risk percentage, and more attributable cases than the western coastal region. CONCLUSION: There was significant spatial heterogeneity, autocorrelation, and clustering in the associations between short-term exposure to PM2.5 and daily reported confirmed COVID-19 cases across the contiguous United States.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to determine the efficacy of nebulised interferon-β1a (SNG001) in patients with Coronavirus disease-2019 (COVID-19). METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and clinicaltrials.gov, without language restrictions. Studies were searched up to November 2025. Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) on treatment of COVID-19 with SNG001, compared with placebo or standard of care, were reviewed. Data were analysed using the RevMan Version 5.1 (The Cochrane Collaboration). Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated for dichotomous outcomes. RESULTS: Four RCTs (enrolling 1055 participants) met the inclusion criteria. The proportion of patients with hospitalisations (data extracted from two RCTs) (RR 0.16, 95% CI 0.03 to 0.88), and serious adverse events (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.47 to 0.90) were significantly fewer in SNG001 groups. There was no statistically significant difference in all-cause mortality (RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.37 to 1.39), patients non-recovery at day 28 (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.65 to 1.17), and adverse event (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.04) between the two groups. CONCLUSIONS: Nebulised SNG001 was safe and associated with a reduction in COVID-19-related hospital admission. SNG001 shows a potential benefit for outpatients with COVID-19, but it requires larger clinical trials for future validations, particularly in vaccinated and previously infected populations.

papers.abstract_en: BackgroundIdiopathic pleuroparenchymal fibroelastosis (iPPFE) is a rare, progressive interstitial lung disease with a poor prognosis and no established pharmacological treatment. Cachexia and cachexia-related symptoms are common in patients with iPPFE and are associated with functional decline and poor outcomes.ObjectivesTo evaluate the efficacy and safety of anamorelin, an oral ghrelin receptor agonist, in patients with iPPFE.DesignProspective interventional study.MethodsIn this single-arm pilot study, patients with iPPFE received oral anamorelin hydrochloride (100 mg once daily) for 8 weeks. The primary endpoint was the change in anorexia- and cachexia-related symptoms assessed using the Anorexia/Cachexia Subscale of the Functional Assessment of Anorexia/Cachexia Therapy (FAACT-A/CS). Exploratory endpoints included changes in body weight, lean body mass, nutritional biomarkers, dyspnoea severity, respiratory-related quality of life (QOL), and handgrip strength. Safety was assessed through clinical and laboratory evaluations.ResultsNineteen patients were enrolled; 18 received at least one dose of anamorelin, and 15 were included in the efficacy analyses. The median FAACT-A/CS score increased from 26 to 36, with a Hodges-Lehmann estimate of 5.0 (95% confidence interval, 0.5-9.5) (p = 0.028). Body weight, lean body mass, prealbumin, and transferrin levels increased from baseline. Circulating growth hormone (GH) and insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) levels also increased. Dyspnoea severity decreased, respiratory-related QOL scores increased, and handgrip strength increased. No treatment-related serious adverse events occurred; however, two participants discontinued treatment because of treatment-related adverse events (hepatic enzyme elevation and generalised oedema).ConclusionTreatment with anamorelin was associated with improvements in cachexia-related symptoms, body weight, body composition, nutritional biomarkers, respiratory-related QOL, and pharmacodynamic effects on the GH/IGF-1 axis in patients with iPPFE. Given the potential attrition bias, these exploratory findings warrant cautious interpretation and confirmation in randomised controlled trials.

papers.authors: Memarian M, Mahdavi M, Bitaraf M, Paknazar F, Yaribeygi H
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Internal Medicine, School of Medicine, Semnan University of Medical Sciences, Semnan, Iran.
papers.results: 治疗3个月后：FEV1显著改善（P < 0.001）；MMEF显著改善（P = 0.019）；FEV1/FVC比值变化无统计学意义（P = 0.106）；CRP显著下降（P = 0.007）；ESR下降无统计学意义（P = 0.108）；SpO2显著改善（P = 0.033）；六分钟步行距离显著改善（P < 0.001）；CAT评分显著改善（P < 0.001）；体重显著下降（P < 0.001）；HbA1c显著下降（P = 0.004）。摘要未报告各指标效应量、95%CI或绝对变化值。
papers.authors_conclusion: 恩格列净治疗与共病COPD和T2DM患者肺功能、运动能力、COPD症状负担、炎症状态、血糖控制及体重的显著改善相关；这些发现提示恩格列净可能提供降糖之外的临床相关获益，可代表该人群中有前景的治疗选择，仍需更大规模对照研究加以证实。
papers.ai_note: 信息不足：摘要未报告任何效应量、95%CI或绝对变化数值，仅给P值，无法判断临床意义大小。单臂无对照前后设计，所有终点均为干预前后自身比较，无法排除疾病自然波动、回归均值、安慰剂效应及同期稳定降糖治疗的共同作用；前后比较还易受COPD季节性与肺功能重复测量变异影响。样本量仅31例且未见样本量估算。多终点（至少10项）逐一检验未提及多重比较校正，P=0.019、0.033、0.007等边缘结果在多重比较下可能失去意义。次要/替代终点（CRP、体重、HbA1c）与肺功能改善之间无因果链证据，体重与HbA1c改善本身即可解释运动耐量与症状评分变化。作者结论中'clinically relevant benefits'与'promising therapeutic option'属乐观表述，与自身承认需更大规模对照研究的限定并存。

papers.reason: 提示SGLT2抑制剂对COPD合并T2DM人群可能存在肺功能与运动耐量获益，可作为该共病人群治疗决策的假说来源与后续对照研究设计的参考；因缺乏对照与效应量，不能直接用于临床决策，也不涉及胸科肿瘤业务核心。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) frequently coexist and are associated with increased morbidity, systemic inflammation, impaired exercise capacity, and reduced quality of life. Beyond glycemic control, empagliflozin has demonstrated anti-inflammatory and metabolic benefits that may potentially improve respiratory outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of empagliflozin on pulmonary function, inflammatory markers, exercise capacity, and COPD-related symptoms in patients with coexisting COPD and T2DM. METHODS: A prospective, single-arm, before-and-after interventional study was conducted in 31 patients with coexisting COPD and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Participants received empagliflozin (10 mg/day) for three months in addition to their stable antidiabetic therapy. Pulmonary function, inflammatory markers, oxygen saturation, six-minute walk distance, COPD Assessment Test (CAT) score, body weight, and HbA1c were evaluated at baseline and after treatment. Changes in outcome measures were compared between the two time points. RESULTS: After three months of treatment, significant improvements were observed in FEV1 (P < 0.001) and MMEF (P = 0.019), whereas the change in FEV1/FVC ratio was not statistically significant (P = 0.106). CRP levels decreased significantly (P = 0.007), while ESR showed a non-significant reduction (P = 0.108). Significant improvements were also observed in SpO2 (P = 0.033), six-minute walk distance (P < 0.001), and CAT score (P < 0.001). Furthermore, empagliflozin significantly reduced body weight (P < 0.001) and HbA1c levels (P = 0.004). CONCLUSION: Empagliflozin therapy was associated with significant improvements in pulmonary function, exercise capacity, COPD symptom burden, inflammatory status, glycemic control, and body weight in patients with coexisting COPD and T2DM. These findings suggest that empagliflozin may provide clinically relevant benefits beyond glucose lowering and could represent a promising therapeutic option in this patient population. Larger controlled studies are needed to confirm these findings.

papers.abstract_en: Noninvasive ventilation (NIV) and high-flow nasal therapy (HFNT) are central to the management of acute and chronic respiratory failure, yet their monitoring remains largely descriptive and reactive. Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to transform this paradigm by enabling dynamic, predictive and individualised approaches to respiratory support. This narrative review summarises current knowledge and future perspectives of AI applications in NIV and HFNT monitoring. AI techniques, including supervised and unsupervised machine learning, deep learning, and hybrid approaches, can integrate multimodal data across different timescales, from high-frequency ventilator signals to longitudinal telemonitoring data. Current applications include early detection of treatment failure, outcome prediction, patient phenotyping and automated detection of patient-ventilator asynchrony. While these approaches have shown promising performance in retrospective and proof-of-concept studies, their implementation in routine clinical practice remains limited. Key challenges include data heterogeneity, limited sample sizes, insufficient external validation and issues related to interpretability and integration into clinical workflows. Regulatory and ethical considerations further highlight the need to ensure transparency, safety and clinician trust. Future developments are expected to move towards adaptive and closed-loop systems capable of continuously optimising respiratory support. Ultimately, AI should be viewed as a tool to augment clinical expertise, supporting a shift towards more anticipatory, personalised and responsive respiratory care.

papers.abstract_en: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is a life-limiting autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic loss-of-function mutations in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) gene, most commonly F508del. Mutant CFTR disrupts transepithelial ion transport and intracellular redox homeostasis, leading to excessive accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS). Evidence from cohort studies, human airway organoid models, and single-cell transcriptomic analyses published between 2020 and 2026 has prompted substantial revision of the prevailing linear model of CF pathogenesis. These studies demonstrate that misfolded CFTR can independently initiate oxidative stress and low-grade inflammation in the absence of microbial colonization. Mitochondrial ROS (mitoROS) constitute a central signaling hub linking F508del-induced protein misfolding to transcriptional suppression of the Nrf2 antioxidant program, constitutive activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, and dysregulation of TLR-cytokine cascades. Triple CFTR modulator regimens, including elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor (ETI) and the once-daily combination vanzacaftor/tezacaftor/deutivacaftor (Alyftrek, FDA-approved December 2024 for patients ≥6 years carrying at least one F508del or other Alyftrek-responsive CFTR variant; pivotal SKYLINE 102/103 trials demonstrated non-inferiority versus ETI in largely ETI-eligible populations), have transformed clinical care. However, multi-omics data indicate that these agents do not fully restore airway redox homeostasis or resolve persistent low-grade inflammation, even when CFTR channel activity recovers to 40%-50% of wild-type levels. This incomplete recovery may reflect persistent epigenetic inflammatory memory, uncorrected mitochondrial dysfunction, and incomplete restoration of the non-channel functions of CFTR. Moreover, marked interindividual variability in modulator response and persistent nonresponse underscore the need for adjunctive strategies. This review integrates foundational mechanistic studies with recent findings to delineate how CFTR regulates ROS-dependent tissue injury and immune dysregulation and to assess redox-targeted combination therapies designed to complement CFTR modulator monotherapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Respiratory viruses remain a major global public health concern and are among the leading causes of acute respiratory infections worldwide. University students, particularly healthcare students, represent a potentially important group for viral circulation because of frequent social interaction and exposure to clinical environments. Evidence regarding respiratory virus circulation in university populations from Latin America, especially Ecuador, remains limited. OBJECTIVE: To estimate the prevalence of respiratory viruses among 438 healthcare university students in three Ecuadorian cities and to describe the proportion of infections detected in students without symptoms. METHODS: A multicenter cross-sectional study based on a convenience sample was conducted between January 4 and February 3, 2026, among healthcare university students from universities located in Quito, Guayaquil, and Cuenca, Ecuador. Nasopharyngeal samples were analyzed on site using a combo rapid antigen test for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), Influenza A, Influenza B, and Adenovirus. Sociodemographic and epidemiological variables were recorded. Exact tests and exploratory Firth penalized logistic regression were used to explore factors associated with positivity. RESULTS: Fourteen participants tested positive for at least one respiratory virus, corresponding to an overall prevalence of 3.2% (95% CI: 1.8-5.3). Influenza A virus and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) were the most frequent single detections (n = 4 each), followed by adenovirus (n = 3). Three coinfections were identified. Eight of the 14 positive participants (57.1%) were asymptomatic, whereas six (42.9%) reported respiratory symptoms. A significant association was identified between symptom presence and viral detection (p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Respiratory virus detection among healthcare university students in Ecuador was low, and more than half of the positive students reported no symptoms, suggesting that these viruses may circulate unnoticed within university environments. Because rapid antigen tests have limited sensitivity and do not directly measure infectivity, the true prevalence is probably higher, and studies with molecular confirmation, larger samples, and longer sampling periods are needed. Rapid antigen tests were operationally feasible as point-of-care tools for on-site screening in academic environments.

papers.abstract_en: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by members of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC), remains a major global health challenge, with over 10 million new cases and more than 1 million deaths reported annually. Ten distinct human-adapted MTBC lineages circulate worldwide, contributing to the pathogen's remarkable evolutionary success. Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) have emerged as key molecular regulators that can influence pathogen survival, immune responses, and disease progression. For the pathogen, ncRNAs regulate virulence, stress adaptation, metabolism, dormancy, persistence, and drug tolerance, thereby enabling it to survive hostile host environments. In the host, ncRNAs modulate critical immune processes, including macrophage activation, cytokine production, inflammation, cell death pathways, and antigen presentation. Advances in next-generation sequencing and transcriptomics have accelerated the discovery of ncRNA-mediated regulatory networks involved in TB pathogenesis and host-pathogen interactions. Experimental studies have demonstrated the immunoregulatory roles of host ncRNAs in shaping protective and pathological responses to M. tuberculosis infection, while mycobacterial ncRNAs have been linked to adaptation, virulence, and antibiotic resistance. In this review, we provide an integrated, cross-kingdom overview of host-derived ncRNAs, including miRNAs, lncRNAs, and circRNAs, as well as M. tuberculosis-encoded sRNAs. We highlight their roles in immune regulation, TB pathogenesis, and pathogen adaptation, as well as their potential as diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets. We summarize current knowledge of their biogenesis and expression patterns during M. tuberculosis infection and examine the regulatory mechanisms through which ncRNAs modulate host immune responses and bacterial adaptation strategies, ultimately influencing TB disease outcomes. Finally, we discuss the translational relevance of ncRNAs in TB diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment, highlighting key opportunities and challenges to advance their clinical application and improve TB control.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: COPD is a prevalent, progressive respiratory disorder for which cigarette smoking represents the predominant modifiable risk factor. To distinguish metabolites merely indicative of tobacco exposure from those specifically associated with incipient COPD-related pathological changes, we employed untargeted ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry to comprehensively profile serum and urine metabolomes in a time-stratified rat model of chronic cigarette smoke exposure. This approach enabled systematic characterization of dynamic, time-dependent metabolic perturbations and facilitated the identification of candidate metabolites linked both to smoke exposure and to early-stage lung injury. METHODS: We set up four groups of rat models treated with smoking method at different times to evaluate and understand the development process of COPD from the onset to the stable stage. The animal models were verified by pathological experiments, and the serum and urine of rats were analyzed by mass spectrometry to compare the changes of urine and serum metabolites in different periods of smoking. As a first step toward identifying exposure markers and candidate pathology-related metabolites in at-risk smokers, we sought to identify metabolites associated with cigarette smoke exposure and early smoke-induced pulmonary changes. RESULTS: Four candidate metabolites were identified by non-targeted metabolomic analysis, and receiver work characteristics analysis showed that all types of metabolomic data had high predictive power, with area under the curve values exceeding 0.75. These results suggest that the identified metabolites can distinguish cigarette smoke exposure from unexposed conditions and may be associated with COPD-like pulmonary pathology. CONCLUSION: This study profiled serum and urine metabolites in a time-stratified rat model of cigarette smoke-induced lung injury. Using multivariate and univariate analyses with correction for multiple testing, we identified four metabolites associated with smoke exposure and with emerging smoke-induced lung pathology.

papers.abstract_en: Group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s) contribute to type 2 asthma through rapid production of interleukin-5 and interleukin-13, but the inhibitory pathways that restrain pathogenic ILC2 activity remain incompletely defined. Most evidence for programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1)-mediated inhibition of ILC2s comes from murine models, humanized mice, and stimulated or expanded human cells; cell-resolved expression and functional engagement of PD-1 have not been established in freshly isolated airway ILC2s from well-characterized asthma cohorts. In available experimental systems, PD-1 engagement suppresses ILC2 proliferation and cytokine production, whereas programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) displayed by ILC2s can act outwardly on PD-1-positive CD4-positive T cells. Programmed death-ligand 2 (PD-L2) can inhibit isolated ILC2s through PD-1, but its whole-lung effects also involve dendritic-cell IL-12 regulation and RGMb-dependent respiratory tolerance. Interpretation therefore depends on the ligand-bearing and responding cells, ligand form, tissue compartment, disease stage, and asthma endotype. This review examines cell-intrinsic PD-1 signaling, ligand-specific cellular interactions, immunometabolic regulation, and translational constraints. The current evidence supports preclinical investigation rather than clinical readiness; direct validation in human airway ILC2s, definition of receptor-proximal signaling, and a predictive biomarker are prerequisites for therapeutic development.
